text:
anika: heads up — noticed a small but consistent MRR drop in the longdoc slice after we promoted quant-v2 last night. baseline v1 -> v2 A/B shows -1.7% overall, but longdoc slice is -3.9% :frowning:

sam: ugh. did the auto-fallback trigger?

eli: deploy-bot says promote completed at 1799988000, no auto-fallback logged. i pulled the per-slice evals:
```
{"slice":"longdoc","v1_mrr":0.278,"v2_mrr":0.267,"delta":-0.011}
{"slice":"short-answer","v1_mrr":0.412,"v2_mrr":0.413,"delta":+0.001}
{"slice":"legal-summary","v1_mrr":0.301,"v2_mrr":0.289,"delta":-0.012}
```

jia: interesting — latency looks fine, p95 +1ms. quality-only regression. what were our fallback thresholds?

anika: config: fallback if aggregate MRR drop > 2% AND any weighted-slice delta < -2.5% OR slice count * 0.5 effect size > threshold. basically it requires a strong signal to avoid flip-flopping.

sam: so longdoc at -3.9 should have tripped? unless weight on that slice is tiny in the composite. eli — can you paste the slice weights?

eli: pasted from rollout config: `slices: {longdoc:0.05, short-answer:0.6, legal-summary:0.02, conversation:0.33}` — longdoc weight low so global delta didn't exceed 2%.

anika: thanks. sounds like the low-weighted but high-impact slice was essentially ignored by auto-fallback. we should either adjust weights or add a hard fail for any slice <-3% if it has >1000 requests/day.

jia: agree. proposal: add per-slice absolute cutoff: if slice delta < -3% AND slice qps > X => immediate rollback. also add smoothing window shrink: current window = 6h, reduce to 2h for first 12h post-promote.

sam: sg. can we run an ablation to see if user-visible metrics (CTR/retention proxies) correlate with longdoc MRR? want to avoid oscillation for small noise.

eli: ran a quick query. longdoc covers ~1.2k requests/day for affected route (0.04% of total), but these are high-value workflows (legal customers). short-term retention proxy shows 0.8% drop for that cohort last 24h.

anika: decision: pause further promotion ramp; create a hotfix to add per-slice absolute cutoff and reduce smoothing window. fallback policy updated to: `if any_slice.delta_pct <= -3.0 AND slice_qps >= 500 => immediate fallback` and `global_mrr_drop >= 1.8% over 2h => fallback`.

sam: can you open a quick PR for the fallback rules and a changelog entry? tag me for quick review.

anika: sure. PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/rollouts/pulls/412 (draft) — includes tests and new config schema.

deploy-bot: canary-promote quant-v2 -> 50% completed at 1799989000.

eli: test plan: run `rb eval --model quant-v2 --slices longdoc,legal-summary --metrics mrr,bleu --window 2h` and smokecheck against heldout examples. also run the contrastive judge harness on 2k longdoc pairs.

jia: please also add an alert in datadog: `redwood.rollout.slice.delta` with threshold -2.5% over 30m to a new incident channel eng-oncall until we stabilize.

sam: noted. i'll add the monitor and set sensitivity low for 48h to avoid noisy paging.

anika: timeline: hotfix PR -> review by sam (1h), merge -> rollout-policy deploy (ops-bot) -> observe for 4h then either resume ramp or rollback. if hotfix merges, ops-bot should annotate rollout with new policy id.

ops-bot: rollout-policy update queued. apply-on-merge: true.

eli: running the eval now, will paste outputs if anything else shows up.

anika: thanks all. main takeaway — low-weighted longtail slices can hide customer-impacting regressions; we need absolute per-slice fail-safes for high-value slices.

sam: +1. follow up doc? we should capture this as a pattern for future promos.

jia: i'll draft a short runbook entry after we confirm the mitigation.

eli: eval done — longdoc contrastive judge: v1 wins 64% over v2 on sampled pairs (2k). attaching quick diff: https://notebooks.redwood.ai/longdoc-quantv2-diff (internal).

anika: rollforward paused. i'll ping legal-customer-ops if the rollback happens.
